government.note: On 1 January 2000 Pakistan was under the military government formed after the coup of 12 October 1999: General Pervez Musharraf held executive power as Chief Executive, the constitution was held in abeyance and the National Assembly, Senate and provincial assemblies were suspended; Rafiq Tarar remained President until 20 June 2001, when Musharraf took the presidency. A general election in October 2002 restored an elected National Assembly and prime minister. Pakistan is otherwise a federal parliamentary republic. The prime-minister office below also carries Musharraf's tenure as Chief Executive (1999-2002), when the office of prime minister was vacant, so that the head-of-government timeline is continuous.

system.note: seats_2000 is the result of the February 1997 election (207 general seats by first-past-the-post plus 10 minority seats); the assembly was suspended after the October 1999 coup. From 2002 the house has 342 seats (272 general seats by first-past-the-post plus 60 reserved for women and 10 for non-Muslims, allocated proportionally to parties); 336 from 2024. The 1997 results table gives PML(N) 135 seats; the infobox gives 137.

chambers.review_note: The 1997 results table and infobox disagree on PML(N) seats (135 vs 137). Others = PPP (Shaheed Bhutto) 1, NPP 1, Jamhoori Wattan Party 2 and the 10 minority seats.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate, because the elected assemblies were suspended. Based on the February 1997 National Assembly vote: PML(N) 44.9% and PML(J) 3.2% (liberal conservative, reduced to 0.43 to allow for support for the military government); PPP 21.3% and PPP (Shaheed Bhutto) 1.9% (social democrat); MQM 3.9%, ANP 1.8%, BNP, JWP and other regional parties about 1.5% (regionalist); JUI(F) 1.7% and other religious parties (Islamist, raised to 0.05 for parties that did not stand or won few votes); PTI 1.6% (Islamic democrat); independents 13.8% and minority-seat votes 2.2% (big tent). The military_junta share is a gameplay estimate of support for the military government.

claims.note: Pakistan claims most of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, including the Indian-administered areas.
